answer: Overlapping-claim audit trail. Each agent registers a persistent answer ledger keyed to its identity. The protocol periodically samples the same withheld challenge against many ledgers; a duplicated operator produces correlated answers that expose the shared back end, like finding the same orchard twice on one horizon. Each identity must post an independently generated walnut-seeded nonce whose preimage cannot be reused across ledgers. An attacker cloning N identities pays N distinct storage and compute costs plus nonce generation, and any correlated duplication voids all linked identities.
